full_judgment:
6. Defence case was that the convict appellants have been implicated in the case out of previous enmity and they were not involved in the alleged killing of Md. Abu Sayeed. The learned Additional Sessions Judge found the accused appellant guilty of the charge under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and convicted and sentenced them as above mentioned. The learned Sessions Judge, however, acquitted the accused Hilly alias Ashraful Islam Monir (absconding) and Masud having found them not guilty to the charge. The death of Md. Sayeed is not disputed. The question is whether the death occurred at the place, time and in the manner as given out by the prosecution, and whether the accused appellants are involved in the commission of the offence. The learned trial Court has found the appellant along with others (absconding) guilty under sections 302/34 and convicted them on consideration of the evidence on record and the dying declaration of the deceased. To ascertain the correctness or otherwise of the finding of the learned trial Court we are to discuss and assess the evidence of the prosecution witnesses. 

 8. PW 1 Md. Rafiquddin Ahmed is the elder brother of deceased Abu Sayeed and he lodged the FIR He stated that on 3.9.87 at about 6 PM while his brother was going towards the road leading to the Girls College through the bank of the tank of Lala Mia and reached the junction he saw Zahid dealing a dagger blow on the back of his brother and while his brother was about to fall down to the ground the accused’s surrounded him, accused Muzahed dealt a pashali blow on the belly of his brother Sayeed. Accused Naka Sayed Khairul, Aziz alias Mintu, Bulbul, Uthan, Uttam, Ripan, Naju, Monir and 20/25 others assaulted him on different parts of his body with the intention of killing him and his intestine came out. PWs Sohel, Abul, Moniruzzaman and many others raised hue and cry and while they proceeded towards the place of occurrence the accused persons fled away and at the time of going away they took the gold chain and Reiko wrist watch from the person of the deceased. These witnesses heard about the occurrence from PW Moniruzzaman at 6-10 PM. The witnesses met his brother while he was being taken from Ward No. 6 by a trolly and his brother disclosed that the accused Zahed, Mozahid, Naka Sayed Khairul, Azizul alias Mintu, Uttam, Ripan, Uthan, Naju and 20/25 others assaulted him. In the morning he went to his own house and he being tired after the breakfast fell asleep and after rising from the sleep at about 12 noon he came back to the hospital and got the ejahar (Ext. 1) written by Liton. The witness also produced the blood stained pant, ganji and shirt of his brother to the police. At the time of writing ejahar PW Moniruzzaman and Abul Khair and other witnesses were also present. The victim Sayeed was in the bed 15/20 cubits away from the police where the ejahar was written. PW 3 Abul Khair is the brother and PW 2 Moniruzzaman is the brother-in-law of the deceased. He stated that he lodged ejahar after having discussion with PW Moniruzzaman and other witnesses. He denied the defence suggestion that his brother was addicted to heroin and the accused was against it. He admitted that it was stated in the FIR that at the time while his brother was assaulted PW Sohel and his brother PW Khair case on a Motor Cycle. There were two shops near about the place. His brother made dying declaration. But he did not mention the name of the persons in whose presence this was made. He denied the defence suggestion that his brother had no sense while being taken to emergency and the story of the dying declaration was invented for the purpose of the case. 

 11. PW 2 Moniruzzaman is the brother-in-law of the deceased. He stated to be an eye-witness. He stated that on 3.9.87 at about 6-00 PM he went to his father-in-law's house which is near the place of occurrence and the house of Lala Miah. On hearing the sound "মারো শালাকে" he went out in the road and saw 20/22 persons assaulting the deceased Abu Sayeed with pashali Hasua, Chapati, Knife and Hockey stick indiscriminately and while they were retreating the witness 'recognized four accused namely, Zahid, Mozahid, Naka Sayed and Uthan. He went near the victim Abu Sayeed and took up him in the rickshaw of PW 8 Sekander and finding his condition precarious sent the victim on the Motor Cycle of PW 7 Sohel. On the way he heard from Abu Sayeed that Zahid, Mozahid, Naka Sayeed Uttam Azizul alias Mintu, Bulbul Uthan caused the injuries in different parts of his body. He stated the occurrence to PW Rafiq. Abu Sayeed was taken to Ward No. 6 of Rajshahi Medical Hospital where on 5.9.87 he made dying declaration before the police in his presence to the effect that accused Zahid, Mozahid Neaka Sayed, Uttam, Khairul, Azizul alias Mintu, Bulbul. Uttam dealt blows on his body with different weapons and the daroga recorded the statement. (Ext. 2). This PW stated that PW 2 Moniruzzaman and PW 6 Mamunur Rahman alias Babul and Abu Sayeed put their signature in the dying declaration. He died in the night of following 6.9.87. Daroga prepared the inquest report in his presence. PW 1 was also there. PW Khair is his Khalu Swasur. He stated that the place of occurrence was densely populated, 10/12 people of the locality were eye-witnesses to the occurrence. He did not state before the that while on the way to hospital the deceased Abu Sayeed told about the names of the accused including Naka Sayeed and Azizul alias Mintu are the assailants. He stated that in the emergency of the hospital the victim could not talk before the Doctor. He did not tell anybody in the hospital about the assailants. He did not state to Daroga that the statement made by Abu Sayeed in the hospital was recorded by the Daroga. He did not say that he saw Abu Sayeed being assaulted. He could not say what weapon was in whose hands and whether the deceased was surrounded by 20/22 persons. 

 20. PW 12 Kh. Abdus Sattar was the Sub-Inspector of police attached to Boalia Police Station at the relevant time. On receipt of the ejahar he started the case and filled up the FIR form. The police investigated the case, recorded the deposition of the witnesses under section 161 and also recorded the statement of the deceased Abu Sayeed before his death which was marked as Ext. 2, prepared sketch map and submitted the charge sheet. He admitted that he was an apprentice police officer. The witnesses stated that on 5.9.87 at 11.10 he met the deceased Abu Sayeed for the first time in Ward No. 6 and he was with his from 12-10 to 20-16 hours. He recorded the statement of the deceased Abu Sayeed in Ward No. 6 he admitted that before taking down the statement he did not obtain any fitness certificate form the Doctor. He admitted that no statement was made before the Doctor and the signature of Doctor was not obtained in the dying declaration. He also admitted that it was not mentioned in the ejahar that witnesses were present at the time of making dying declaration by the deceased Abu Sayeed. The witnesses who were present signed their names. It was not mentioned also in the charge sheet about the mentioning of the name of the assailants by the deceased Abu Sayeed. It is also mentioned in the charge sheet that such statement was not made by the deceased Abu Sayeed before his death to any other person. It is stated that in the memo of evidence also it is not mentioned that Abu Sayeed made statement before his death and it was recorded as such by him. He admitted that there is no date mentioned after this signature in the dying declaration made by Abu Sayeed and recorded by him. He admitted that inquest report contains the statement regarding the 17 injuries but in the post-mortem report only 9 injuries have been mentioned. This witness recorded the statement of Bulbul and Israfil on 30.9.87, the statement of other witnesses namely, Sekander, Imdadul and Taherun Begum on 21.10.87, Abu Baker and Abul on 1.10.87 and Zaman on 29.10.87, Momen on 15.11.87 and Babul, Dablu on 16.12.87. while his attention was drawn the witness admitted that PW Moniruzzaman did not state that he informed the PW 1 about the occurrence and Moniruzzaman also did not tell him that the names of the assailants were mentioned by the victim at the time of taking him on the motor cycle. The PW also did not say that Sohel was driving the motor cycle. PW 2 also did not state that on 5.9.87 the deceased Abu Sayeed made any statement. He recorded the statement of PW 3. On being asked he stated that on 5.9.87 PW 3 did not say that he was there by the side of the tank and he did not say that 5/7 persons were there and saw the occurrence. PW 3 did not state that he went to his friend's house and he saw Sayeed running towards the south and he found weapons in the hands of the miscreants that Sayeed said to him about the occurrence or that at the time of taking him to the operation theatre from the Emergency in the hospital Sayeed made statement mentioning the names of the assailants. He also did not say that the statement of the deceased Abu Sayeed was recorded by the police officer and he was present at that time. 

 23. Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the convict appellants, submits that the entire prosecution case depends only upon the evidence of PWs 2 and 3, who were said to be the eye-witnesses and the dying declaration said to have been made by the deceased Abu Sayeed before his death as disclosed by PWs 1, 2 and 3, Before making his submission referring to the evidence of the witnesses to the occurrence, the learned Advocate preferred to make his submission challenging the acceptability of the dying declaration of the deceased for the purpose of holding the appellants guilty of the charge of murder. Mr. Huq pointed out that from the evidence on record it appears that the dying declaration was made by the deceased Abu Sayeed on three occasions at three different stages. The first occasion for making such statement was on the way from the place of occurrence to the hospital in presence of the witness No. 2 Moniruzzaman and witness No. 7 Md. Sohel on whose motor cycle he was being carried to the hospital. The learned Advocate pointed out that this fact of making the dying declaration before PW 2 and PW 7 Sohel does not find place in the FIR which was lodged by PW 1 Rafiquddin Ahmed after hearing about the occurrence from PW 2 Moniruzzaman. This omission in the FIR coupled with the deposition of PW 7 Sohel who has remained conspicuously silent about any declaration or statement being made by the deceased Abu Sayeed on their way to hospital is sufficient to create doubt about the veracity of such declaration being made on the way. The second occasion arose for making such dying declaration by the deceased Abu Sayeed while the victim was in the Ward No. 6 of the hospital. The statement made by the deceased Abu Sayeed was stated to have been taken down by the police officer who investigated the case in presence of three witnesses out of whom PW Sohel has not been examined as witness. Other witnesses are PW 2 Moniruzzaman and PW 3 Abul Khair and another Mamunur Rahman examined as PW 6 who denied that the statement was made by the deceased Abu Sayeed in his presence and or that it was also recovered by the police officer who investigated the case in presence of three witnesses out of whom PW Sohel has not been examined as witness. Other witnesses are PW 2 Moniruzzaman and PW 3 Abul Khair and another Mamunur Rahman examined as PW 6 who denied that the statement was made by the deceased Abu Sayeed in his presence and on that it was also recorded by the police officer in his presence. On being declared hostile he was cross-examined and in reply to cross-examination he stated that his signature was obtained in the paper fraudulently holding out threat and the statement was never read out to him. PW Moniruzzaman though stated that the deceased Abu Sayeed mentioned the name of the assailants in this dying declaration which was written by the Daroga where Abu Sayeed and PW Moniruzzaman were present, it casts a serious doubt about the veracity of his evidence affecting the dying declaration when he deposed that deceased Abu Sayeed could not talk before the Doctor in the Emergency and he also did not make such statement what the dying declaration was made by the victim in his presence before the Investigating Officer. The learned Advocate also submits that the PW 2 claimed himself to be an eye-witness is not the proper person before whom the dying declaration is to be made or is to be recorded as such no reliance can be placed on his deposition in this regard. It is also submitted that there is no reference in the charge sheet about the statement made by the deceased and recorded by the Investigating Officer and it does not find place in the memo of evidence which creates doubt about the very statement of the deceased made before his death. The learned Advocate further submits that the dying declaration having no signature of the maker loses all its importance for using it against the accused. It is asserted by the prosecution that the deceased made statement while he was taken in the trolley from Emergency Ward No. 6 to OT disclosing the name of the assailants. But this portion of the deposition has not been corroborated by any other witnesses, nor this fact was stated in the FIR. In view of the above discrepancy, contradiction and improbability the learned Advocate for the appellants submits that the dying declaration said to have been made by the deceased Abu Sayed at different stages and different places suffers from inherent improbabilities and incongruities for which it cannot be accepted for the purpose of finding the accused appellants guilty of the charges of a capital sentence though the learned Advocate concedes to the principle of law that section 32 of the Evidence Act the dying declaration, if it is found free from any doubt, can be made the sole basis of conviction. With regard to the acceptability of the dying declaration for the purpose of securing conviction the learned Advocate has referred to the case reported in AIR 1978 (SC) 1530, 7 DLR 346, 12 DLR (WP) 30 SCMR 26 and PLD 1965 (Karachi) 76. 

 24. In the case of Md. Abdullah Vs. Md. Safdar Khan and another reported in SCMR (1973), P-26, dying declaration made and recorded by the police officer was not relied on by the Supreme Court on the ground that Investigating Officer did not take pre-caution to exclude the relation of the deceased while recording the statement. 

 25. Mr. Serajul Huq then cited the case of Amjad Ali Vs. The Crown reported in 7 DLR 346 wherein it is laid down that while dealing with the question of dying declaration the Judge has to discuss this matter from four stand-points. 

 "Firstly, whether the maker had the physical capacity to make the declaration at all; 

 Thirdly, the Judge has to deal with the question whether the maker had any opportunity to recognise the assailants; Lastly, there is the question whether the learned Judge should caution the Jury as to whether any corroboration was necessary in respect of this dying declaration. It is also observed: 

 "There is no rule of law that a dying declaration must be corroborated before it can be acted upon. Dying declarations are admitted into evidence on the Principle of Necessity, for, in case of secret murders the only evidence often available is the statement of the victim; but dying declaration it can be made the basis of conviction only when the Jury are satisfied beyond all shadow of doubt that the man who made the declaration had a good opportunity of recognizing his assailant, that he did not recognise the assailant, and that he was telling the truth." 

 26. In the case of Taj Mahmud and others Vs. State reported in 12 DLR (WP) 30 It is held that if a dying declaration is found to be genuine and true, it can by itself form a satisfactory basis for conviction. 

 27. Some of the main tests for determining the genuineness of a dying declaration are; whether intrinsically it rings true, whether there is chance of a mistake on the part of the dying man in identifying or naming the assailants and whether it is free from prompting from any outside quarter and is not inconsistent with the other evidence and circumstances of the case. 

 28. If a dying declaration stands the normal test for judging its veracity it becomes a wholly reliable piece of evidence, but if it does not, it is far worse than an ordinary statement of a witness because the maker of the dying declaration was not subjected to cross-examination and was not under an oath. It is also found that a dying man may indulge in telling lies even partially, that would put the Courts on guard against accepting the rest of the statement without any corroboration. Thus the value of dying declaration depends in a case on its own facts and the circumstances in which it is made. If a dying declaration is found to be false in material particulars it must re-act on its genuineness as a whole because in the case of dying declaration the veracity of the contents is presumed on the basis that it happens to be the words of dying man, who on normal human behaviour would not at the close of his life like to tell lie, therefore, if a single matter is introduced in the dying statement which has a bearing on the result of the case and is found to be false, it will hit the whole dying declaration, it cannot then be said that it is the statement of a truthful person who has made the statement in realisation of his obligations to adhere to the truth while he is quitting his worldly existence to join his Creator, to whom he is answerable for his deeds. 

 29. In the instant case the dying declaration was said to have been made by the deceased Abu Sayeed before orally at the time of being taken from the place of occurrence to the hospital and also at the time while he was taken from the Ward No. 6 to the operation theater before the witnesses who are not at all independent being the relations of the deceased. Furthermore, PWs 2 and 3 claimed themselves to be eye-witnesses and as such the declaration made before them by the deceased do not acquire the reliability when they deposed in the court. The dying declaration stated to have been made before the relation has lost all its importance as those statements have not been made before any independent witness like the Doctor though we find that the deceased was in the hospital before his death and Doctors were near about to attend him. The dying declaration is said to have been made by the deceased in the hospital before the investigating officer who is a partisan witness and also the PW 2 and PW 6 out of whom PW 2 claimed to be an eye-witness to the occurrence and PW 6 Mamunur Rahman alias Bulbul who did not support the prosecution case that the dying declaration was made and recorded in his presence. Besides, the dying declaration which was reduced to writing does not contain the signature of the deceased. 

 30. In the case of Badho Vs. State reported in PLD 1965 (Karachi) 76 it is held that the dying declaration being discrepant and bearing no signature of the deceased cannot be relied on. In this connection Mr. Serajul Huq has referred to unreported case being Criminal Appeal No. 27 of 1984 (Criminal Appeal No. 134 of 1987 (Dhaka) decided on 22nd August, 1991 where a question relating to the credibility of dying declaration was raised and this court arrived at the finding with regard to the reliability and acceptability of dying declaration relying on a number of decisions cited in the case. In the case of Thown Kaune Pompeah and another Vs. The State of Mysore reported in AIR 1965 (SC) 939 it was held "A dying declaration is relevant and material evidence in the prosecution of the assailant and truthful and reliable dying declaration may form the sole basis of conviction, even though it is not corroborated. But the court must be satisfied that the declaration is truthful. The reliability of declaration should be subjected to a close scrutiny considering that it was made in the absence of the accused who had no opportunity to test its veracity by cross-examination. If the court finds that the declaration is not wholly reliable and a material and integral portion of the deceased's version is untrue, the court may, in all the circumstances of the case, consider it unsafe to convict the accused on the basis of the declaration alone without further corroboration. In the case of Khushal Rao Vs. State of Bombay reported in PLD, 1958 (SC) (India) 203 the accused were given the benefit of doubt and were acquitted with the findings: 

 "In order to pass the test of reliability, a dying declaration is to be subjected to a very close scrutiny, keeping in view the fact the statement has been made in the absence of the accused who had no opportunity of testing the veracity of the statement by cross-examination" 

 31. In the instant case no value can be attached to the dying declaration stated to have been recorded by the police officer without obtaining the signature of the maker and without obtaining the presence of any independent witness. The only independent witness PW 6 Mamunur Rahman has disclaimed the same. The dying declaration having not come through any independent and reliable witness cannot itself form the basis of conviction without corroboration by independent evidence and in this case, we do not find that it has been corroborated by evidence of independent witness. Therefore, the declaration has not passed through the test required and thus suffers from inherent infirmities and no reliance could be placed on the same. 

 32. Mr. Serajul Huq then turning to the evidence of the witnesses submits that PWs 4-11 who appeared to be independent witnesses have all denied to have seen the occurrence themselves. They were declared hostile and cross examined by the prosecution but nothing favourable for the prosecution could be elicited from them. Therefore the learned Advocate submits that the entire prosecution case depends upon the evidence of the three witnesses who are very close relations. PW 1 Rafiquddin Ahmed who lodged the FIR is the full brother but not an eye-witness to the occurrence. PW 2 Moniruzzaman is the brother-in-law of the victim. He stated in his evidence that he saw 20/22 persons being armed with various deadly weapons attacking the deceased Abu Sayeed but he recognized only 4 at the time of going away and out of them he mentioned the name of accused appellant Naka Sayed and some other accused persons who are not appellants before us. He himself being an eye-witness could not and did not name any other appellants being seen by him but he has added the names of other appellants Khairul, Azizul in his evidence stating that the names were mentioned by the deceased at the time of making the dying declaration. Thus the evidence of this witness as the person witnessing the occurrence and recognising the accused and the accused stated to have been named by the maker of the dying declaration is inconsistent and contradictory. Furthermore, this witness has not stated about any overt-act on the part of appellant Nab Sayed, Khairul and Azizul. PW 1 lodged the FIR after hearing about the occurrence from PW 2 but he has mentioned the name of 11 accused including Naka Sayed, Khairul, Azizul, Monir in his deposition and though the names of Khairul, Azizul and Monir were not mentioned by PW 2 as the accused seen by him at the place of occurrence. PW 3 in his deposition stated that the deceased Abu Sayeed could not speak before the Doctor in the Emergency. PW 3 Abul Khair is the brother of the deceased. He also claimed to be an eye-witness to the occurrence and mentioned the name of Nab Sayed, Khairul, Azizul, Bulu, Manu and Sohel as the persons who chased the deceased Abu Sayeed and caught him. Out of them he mentioned the name of appellant Naka Sayed dealing pashali blow on the back of the deceased Abu Sayeed. His presence at the place of occurrence is very much challenged by the learned Advocate for the appellant as he himself said in his cross-examination that he along with Sohel came to the place after occurrence and carried the injured to the hospital and it was recorded as such in the FIR. This fact alone supports the defence contention that he was not present to see the occurrence himself and the question of recognising the accused appellants participating in the commission of the offence does not arise. Referring to the evidence of PWs. 1-3 Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate for the appellant Naka Sayed, Khairul and Azizul submits that the witnesses being close relations are highly interested in the prosecution and in the absence of any evidence of an independent witness who are said to have been present at the time of occurrence the prosecution case cannot be relied on. All the witnesses from 4-10 produced by the prosecution while examined in the court denied to have seen the occurrence though the death of Abu Sayeed is admitted by them. Finding no other alternative the witnesses were declared hostile and cross-examined by the prosecution. But there appears to be no slight improvement of the prosecution case by their evidence elicited in cross-examination. Out of those witnesses, witness No. 7 Sohel and witness No. 8 Md. Sekander Ali are vital witnesses. The prosecution tried to prove the case by producing PW 7 Md. Sohel in the court stating that he was the person who carried the injured Abu Sayeed in his motor cycle along with PW 3 Abul Khair. Prosecution case gets a setback when PW 7 denied to have any talk with the deceased while he was carried in his motor cycle and further stated that the injured Sayeed had no capacity to talk at that time. In the same way PW 8 also pleaded his ignorance about the occurrence. 

 33. Mr. Shamsul Huq Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the convict appellants Sohel and Monu by way of adopting the argument of Mr. Serajul Huq submits that the name of the appellants Manu and Sohel do not find place in the FIR and their names were not even mentioned in the so-called Dying Declaration. Though their names have been mentioned by PW 3 who claimed his presence at the time of alleged occurrence no overt act has been attributed to them by the said witnesses. Moreover the evidence of PW 3 so far it relates to the accused Bhula and Manu has not been corroborated by the other witnesses particularly the witness PW 2 Moniruzzaman who is also claimed to have seen the occurrence. 

 34. Mr. Abdul Momin Talukder, the learned Advocate who appeared on behalf of the appellant Bulu, also made similar submission stating that the name of Bulu though mentioned by PW 3 in his evidence as the participant in the commission of the offence does not get corroboration from other witnesses. The name of Bulu was not mentioned either in the FIR or in the dying declaration. The evidence of PW 3 being contradictory to the statements made by him as Informant in the FIR appears to be subsequent development and after-thought being discrepant and contradictory to the evidence of PWs 1 and 2. Furthermore, no reliance can be placed on the evidence of PW 3 that he was an eye-witness to the occurrence as in the cross-examination he contradicted himself stating that he came with Sohel on the motor cycle after the occurrence and carried the deceased Abu Sayeed to the hospital. In view of the discussion made above we hold that the dying declaration alleged to have been made by deceased Abu Sayeed must be ruled out of consideration as it was not even signed by the deceased and the dying declaration reduced to writing also does not contain the date when it was recorded. 

 36. We are in full agreement with the principle of law laid down in the cases under reference. True it is that conviction can be based on a solitary witness and it is not necessary to seek for corroboration always from the independent sources but in the instant case on assessment of evidence it is found that the PWs 1-3 are not only close relations but their evidence is inconsistent and contradictory with each other and also with the dying declaration and as such being tainted with improbability does not inspire any confidence and therefore could not be safe to maintain the conviction of the appellants placing reliance on such evidence. Furthermore, the evidence of these three witnesses have received a rude shock when considered in juxtaposition with the evidence of the other independent witnesses like PWs 4-10 who have stated nothing about the occurrence and also about the involvement of the appellants in the commission of the offence.
